preconditions.description: The number of servers n is an integer between 1 and 30,000 inclusive.
There are exactly 4n rules provided in the input.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and 1 <= c <= n for a, b, c in rules)
preconditions.description: For every rule (a, b, c), the server indices a, b, and c are valid integers between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(rules.count((a, b, c)) == 1 for a, b, c in rules)
preconditions.description: Each rule is unique in the input list (though the problem guarantees the structure of a_i, b_i, c_i counts, the input list itself is a set of 4n distinct rule definitions indexed 1 to 4n).

preconditions.expression: sum(1 for a, _, _ in rules if a == s) == 4 for s in range(1, n + 1)
preconditions.description: Each server number from 1 to n appears exactly 4 times as the source server a_i in the rules.

preconditions.expression: sum(1 for _, b, _ in rules if b == s) + sum(1 for _, _, c in rules if c == s) == 8 for s in range(1, n + 1)
preconditions.description: Each server number from 1 to n appears exactly 8 times in total as a destination server (either b_i or c_i) across all rules.

postconditions.description: The output is either a single line 'NO' or two lines starting with 'YES' followed by the sequence.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'NO' or (set(map(int, output_lines[1].split())) == set(range(1, 4 * n + 1)) and len(output_lines[1].split()) == 4 * n)
postconditions.description: If 'YES' is printed, the second line contains a permutation of all rule indices from 1 to 4n.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'NO' or all(0 <= current_load[s] <= 9 for s in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: If 'YES' is printed, the sequence of rules ensures that at every step of execution, the number of processes on any server s (1 to n) never exceeds 9. The load is calculated by starting with 4 processes per server, and for each rule i in the sequence (a_i, b_i, c_i), decrementing the count for a_i and incrementing for b_i and c_i.

postconditions.expression: output_lines[0] == 'NO' or (output_lines[0] == 'YES' and all(0 <= current_load[s] <= 9 for s in range(1, n + 1)))
postconditions.description: The output 'NO' is printed if and only if no valid permutation of rules exists that satisfies the memory constraint (max 9 processes per server at any time).
